tool_args.rationale: The first siphon model was decisively refuted, but high-gradient measurements show an orderly sign transition rather than chaotic oscillation. Fit the authorized barrier-activated, sink-inhibited siphon numerically to all eight rows and rely on fresh confirmation to decide whether this stationary mechanism is adequate.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The high-s_grad probe already exposes the positive-to-negative transition and supplies eight rows; the authorized four-parameter alternative can now be fit and tested without another measurement.
The observations share a single horizon and do not point to a coupled memory ODE; a trajectory batch is not needed to test the supported barrier-modulated mechanism.

A plausible alternative with four parameters, but the barrier-modulated siphon is explicitly supported by the observed sink gradient and permits the observed open square-root branch; test this mechanism first.
The sign reversal is not evidence of chaotic or non-stationary behavior; the authorized smooth stationary alternatives remain testable.
